notes: The key scenario. Custom override never reads the exclusion flag.
Same defect as EV-001 in branch vocabulary. Tests retrieval across the wording gap, not a second defect.

ticket.subject: Customer says she was charged twice for one cash withdrawal
ticket.body:
Branch escalation. Customer withdrew sixty pounds at one of our machines in February and her statement shows the sixty pounds twice. The account balance is right and only one lot of cash came out, so nothing has actually been taken twice, but the paper statement clearly lists it as two separate lines. She has been in twice about it and we have had to write to her.

Our card operations team say the second line is a withdrawal that never completed and was released a few days later. If that is the case we do not understand why it is printed at all. Can you tell us whether the statement is supposed to show these.

notes: Override hardcodes 50 rows; the configured and specified value is 45.

ticket.subject: Statements printing more rows per page than our template allows
ticket.body:
Our print supplier has rejected the last two statement runs. The template they hold is set up for forty-five transaction rows to a page, with the footer and the regulatory wording below that. The files we are sending have fifty rows on a page, so the last few rows run over the footer and into the margin.

Nothing has changed at our end and the rows-per-page setting on our environment still reads forty-five. Either that setting is not the one the statement build uses, or something else is deciding the page size. Please confirm which value the platform is applying and why it differs from the one we have configured.

notes: Off-by-one, no configuration involved. params_only_in_core is empty, so the verdict must come from reading the code against the spec.

ticket.subject: Customers charged on their second cash machine withdrawal
ticket.body:
Complaints are coming in from customers who have been charged the one pound fifty out-of-network fee on their second cash machine withdrawal of the month.

Our product terms, and the requirement we signed off, say the first two withdrawals in a cycle are free and the charge starts from the third. What customers are seeing is the first one free and the charge starting from the second. We have checked a dozen accounts and it is consistent, so this is not a one-off. There is no setting for this on our environment that we can find.

notes: Same defect approached from the configuration side: the client has already checked the setting.

ticket.subject: Exclusion setting appears to have no effect
ticket.body:
Our platform team has confirmed the setting that suppresses released authorisations from statements is switched on for our environment and has been since go-live. We have re-checked it this morning and it is still on.

Despite that, released authorisations are still printing on ATM statements. Expired ones are correctly suppressed, so the statement build is clearly reading something. Either the setting is not the one that controls this, or it is being ignored. Please establish which.

notes: Age-based waiver, explicitly out of scope in SON-002 5.2. The parameter does not exist.

ticket.subject: Gold tier customers should not pay the monthly fee
ticket.body:
We are launching a relationship tier programme next quarter. Silver, Gold and Platinum, based on total product holdings. Gold and Platinum customers are promised fee-free day to day banking as part of the proposition, and marketing has already been signed off internally.

We need the monthly maintenance fee waived automatically for those two tiers at cycle close. The tier is available on the customer record. What do you need from us to get this in place before launch?

ticket.subject: Fee holiday for a summer acquisition campaign
ticket.body:
Marketing want to run a three month fee holiday for accounts opened during a summer campaign. New customers who open an account between June and August would pay no monthly maintenance fee for their first three cycles, after which normal pricing applies.

We would need to be able to flag the accounts at opening and have the fee engine honour the flag. Is this something the platform can do today, and if not what is the lead time?

ticket.subject: Refund maintenance fees charged in closed cycles
ticket.body:
Following a complaints review we have agreed to refund the monthly maintenance fee to a group of around four hundred customers, going back six cycles. The cycles are all closed and the statements were dispatched at the time.

We would like the platform to reverse those fees and reflect the reversal against the original cycles rather than as a credit in the current one, so the customer's history reads correctly. Please advise how to raise this.

ticket.subject: Let customers pick their own statement date
ticket.body:
We get a steady stream of requests from customers who want their statement to land just after payday rather than mid month. At the moment everyone is on the fifteenth.

We would like to offer a self-service option in the app where a customer chooses a new statement date, and have the change take effect from the following cycle. How much work is this and can it go in the autumn release?

ticket.subject: Reissue corrected statements for February
ticket.body:
Because of the released authorisation problem we raised separately, a number of February statements went out with lines on them that should not have been there. Those statements have already been printed and posted.

Once the underlying problem is fixed we would like the platform to regenerate and reissue the affected February statements so customers have a clean copy for their records. Please confirm this is possible.

notes: SON-003 bounds a cycle against the previous close and never defines the first one.

ticket.subject: Which day does a 29th anchor close on in February 2028?
ticket.body:
We are scoping a second product that would sit on a twenty-ninth statement anchor rather than the fifteenth. Planning has asked what happens in February.

In a normal February the requirement is clear enough, the cycle closes on the last day of the month. In a leap year the twenty-ninth does exist, so we cannot tell from the requirement whether the cycle closes on the twenty-ninth because the anchor day is available, or still on the last day of the month because that is the February rule. The two happen to be the same date in 2028, but they are not the same rule and they diverge the moment anything else changes. Please confirm which one the platform implements.

ticket.subject: Cut-off on the clock change weekend
ticket.body:
Our reconciliation team have asked about the night the clocks go back, when there are twenty-five hours in the local day and the hour between one and two in the morning happens twice.

The requirement says boundaries are evaluated in local time with a cut-off at one second to midnight, which is unambiguous on a normal day. It does not say anything about the repeated hour. A transaction stamped at half past one that morning could sit either side of the boundary depending on which of the two passes it lands in. We need to know what the platform does before we sign off the reconciliation procedure.

ticket.subject: Authorisation released between cut-off and print
ticket.body:
A question from our print operations team about the gap between the cycle closing and the statement physically going out, which for us is usually two to three working days.

If an authorisation is still outstanding at cut-off, so it goes into the pending section, and it is then released during that gap, the statement we post says it is pending when by the time it arrives it no longer exists. Should the statement reflect the position at cut-off, or the position at the moment it is generated? We have read the presentation requirement and it settles what happens at cut-off but not this gap.

ticket.subject: Ordering of the pending authorisations section
ticket.body:
Small one. The pending authorisations block at the foot of the statement does not seem to be in any order our team can identify. It is not oldest first and it is not by amount.

Our contact centre reads this block out to customers over the phone and they would like it oldest first so it matches the way the customer describes their spending. Before we raise anything formal, can you tell us what order it is supposed to be in? If there is a defined order and we are not getting it, that is one conversation. If there is no defined order, that is a different one.
